doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Take-downs for the BBC and writing commercials
summary: He adapted records for visiting acts at the BBC by ear, and began writing for commercials.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: very simplistically for records and having some success. I was arranging Hot Chocolate stage act. I then started writing for the BBC doing take-downs because I had a very good ear and in those days acts like The Stylistics for example, or country artists would come to England and they wouldn’t bring any music. They probably didn’t have it. They hadn’t been to their recording sessions so if there was a full string section on the record I would have to listen to the record and adapt it for whatever show they were coming to do. So all these things were going on at the same time, and then I started writing for commercials.
You used the word “take-downs.” Are you meaning like using your ear to take something off the record and re-create it?

Yes. I would get a cassette from the record company and first of all I would write down what I heard on the record. And then I would adapt it for whatever show they were going on. So if they went on a variety show and they said we’ve only got two woodwinds or something like that, I would then condense the arrangement to fit that line-up. That was an interesting time.
